newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to face no charges in corruption scandal.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to face no charges in corruption scandal.

text.p: Israeli prosecutors decided on Sunday not to charge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal, saying police recommendations to indict him were based on insufficient evidence.

But the government's future hung in the balance as Netanyahu waited to see how coalition partners reacted to a more than 80-page report into the affair, including a recommendation to indict a key political ally, Aryeh Deri.
"After weighing the evidence we have concluded that we don't have sufficient proof to charge the prime minister," Attorney- General Elyakim Rubinstein said.

Rubinstein said Deri, of the ultra-Orthodox Shas party, could eventually be charged with fraud, breach of trust, extortion and obstruction of justice in connection with the short-lived appointment in January of Roni Bar-On, an activist in Netanyahu's Likud party, as attorney-general.

Prosecutors decided to close the file on Netanyahu, Bar-On and Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi. Rubinstein said Deri would have a chance to challenge the charges in a hearing with prosecutors before an indictment is brought.
The investigation would continue against Netanyahu's director-general Avigdor Lieberman and a Likud booster, David Appel.

An Israel Television report had alleged that Deri, already embroiled in a corruption trial, coerced the Likud-led government to appoint Bar-On, who would then offer him a plea bargain. Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid a public outcry he was a legal lightweight unqualified for the job.

Despite media reports beforehand that prosecutors would be especially critical of the prime minister's handling of the affair, an Israeli official close to the prime minister said: "The language is only very mildly critical as far as I know."

The 47-year-old Netanyahu, elected 11 months ago on a promise to pursue peace with security, last week became the first Israeli prime minister to face a police recommendation he be brought to trial -- on charges of fraud and breach of trust.

Israel's Channel One television had said Deri promised that in return for Bar-On's appointment, his Shas party would support Netanyahu's deal with the Palestinians to pull back Israeli troops in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Netanyahu could still face a rebellion from cabinet ministers who could topple his coalition government if the findings raised serious questions about his integrity.

The scandal has cast a giant shadow over Middle East peacemaking, already in crisis since Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last month and sparked an outburst of violence.

"If mistakes were made here, they were routine political mistakes that were made by governments in the past," Netanyahu's communications chief David Bar-Illan told Reuters. "But what that has to do with any kind of criminal investigation, or let alone indictment, I don't know."
He acknowledged the affair would sap some of the government's energies for a few weeks but did not believe peacemaking would be unduly harmed.
Netanyahu's coalition of mainly right-wing and religious parties holds 66 seats in the 120-member parliament.
Even though Netanyahu is not indicted, the opposition can ask Israel's High Court of Justice to force charges to be brought based on the evidence.
